changes.omniauth_rails_csrf_protection: 1.0.2 → 2.0.1 ('~> 1.0' → '~> 2.0'; only change is dropping ActiveSupport::Configurable under Action Pack 8.1+)
changes.omniauth_google_oauth2: 1.1.3 → 1.2.3 ('~> 1.1' → '~> 1.2'; needs jwt >= 2.9.2, < 4, which is why it waited for this phase)

transitive.bcrypt: 3.1.18 → 3.1.22 (devise-only dependency, moved by bundle update devise)
transitive.base64: 0.3.0 unchanged, but now also a declared dependency of jwt 3

changes.unchanged: omniauth 2.3.1, omniauth-github 2.0.1, omniauth-oauth2 1.10.0, oauth2 2.0.25, warden 1.2.9, orm_adapter 0.5.0 (all already latest)
changes.views:
none — every copied view under app/views/devise is a Bootstrap customisation that never used the
layout, the 'Send me reset password instructions' label, or data-turbo-cache; the gem-shipped views the app still renders uncopied (passwords/edit, shared/_error_messages) only gained

wrappers and data-turbo-temporary, with the same labels the feature specs look for
changes.initializer: config/initializers/devise.rb unchanged — every option it sets still exists in the 5.0.4 generator template; config.responder.error_status/redirect_status left unset (Devise defaults :ok / :found), as no deprecation asked for them
changes.routes: POST /users/auth/:provider only. Devise 5 routes the authorize path with OmniAuth.config.allowed_request_methods ([:post] since Phase 4) where Devise 4 hard-coded GET|POST, so GET /users/auth/:provider is now a routing 404 instead of a 404 from OmniauthCallbacksController#passthru. Callback route still GET|POST. Documented in spec/routing/omniauth_routes_spec.rb

specs_added.spec/services/jwt_token_service_spec.rb: encode/decode round trip, exp claim, expired → ExpiredError, tampered signature/payload, foreign key, alg none, nil/empty/garbage, and the jwt 3 strict-Base64 cases (trailing newline, surrounding whitespace → DecodeError)

verification.devise_secret_key: unchanged in every environment. config/initializers/devise.rb sets config.secret_key = ENV['SECRET_KEY_BASE'] explicitly, so the SecretKeyFinder removal never applies; and Rails.application.secret_key_base, secrets.secret_key_base (config/secrets.yml ← ENV) and Devise.secret_key all resolved to the same value in the container. Outstanding password-reset tokens stay valid
verification.devise_removals: grep of app/ spec/ config/ lib/ before and after: no sign_in(resource, scope) positional, no Devise::TestHelpers (spec/support/initializers/devise.rb already uses Devise::Test::ControllerHelpers), no sign_in bypass: true (Users::ProfilesController uses bypass_sign_in), no devise_error_messages! (removed in #217)
verification.jwt_errors: JWT::ExpiredSignature < ClaimValidationError < TokenError < DecodeError < JWT::Error; JWT::VerificationError < SignatureError < TokenError < DecodeError. JwtTokenService's two rescues still catch everything they did. JWT::EncodeError is not a DecodeError; encode is not rescued and never was — with jwt 3.2+ an empty HMAC key raises JWT::EncodeError ('HMAC key cannot be empty') instead of silently signing, which only happens if SECRET_KEY_BASE is unset, and Rails 7 refuses to boot production without it
verification.deprecations: none from Devise or jwt in the full suite output (config.active_support.deprecation = :stderr in test)
verification.local: arm64 dev image: rubocop 162 files, no offenses; rspec 393 examples, 0 failures, 6 pending (the pre-existing Not yet implemented placeholders)
verification.ci: unit/feature suite plus rubocop on every push (x86_64)
verification.staging: manual Google and GitHub sign-in required before promoting — the smoke suite (spec/smoke/oauth_providers_spec.rb) covers only the authorize redirect and a bogus-code callback, not a real token exchange; omniauth-google-oauth2 1.2.3 changed how it treats ID tokens

held_back.rails_application_secrets: JwtTokenService still reads Rails.application.secrets.secret_key_base; moving to Rails.application.secret_key_base is Phase 6 (Rails 7.1), where it is deprecated
held_back.responder_statuses: config.responder.error_status = :unprocessable_entity / redirect_status = :see_other not adopted; the app has no Turbo and the defaults (200 / 302) are what the feature specs and smoke specs expect

notes.smoke_specs: unchanged. spec/smoke/oauth_providers_spec.rb's GET /users/auth/:provider example only asserts the response does not redirect to the provider, which a routing 404 satisfies; no status, body or path the smoke or request specs assert on changed
